title: Frequentist Calibration Curves with curveRfreq
text: curveR ecosystem consists three packages share common data contract defined curveRcore: curveRcore — preprocessing pipelines, forward model functions, inverse back-calculation functions, analytical gradients, calibration_result S3 class, eligibility-gating logic shared across fitting engines. curveRfreq (package) — frequentist nonlinear least-squares (NLS) calibration via fit_calibration_freq() multi-curve wrapper fit_calibration_freq_multiplate(). curveRbayes — Bayesian calibration via Stan; produces calibration_result object downstream code engine-agnostic. need full frequentist-vs-Bayesian comparison, including LOO-CV model selection posterior predictive checks, see hub vignette vignette("curveR-ecosystem-overview"). vignette covers curveRfreq alone, raw assay data calibrated concentrations per-sample precision.

title: Frequentist Calibration Curves with curveRfreq
text: curveRfreq ships synthetic multi-plate bead-based immunoassay dataset mirrors structure expected fitting pipeline. list contains six elements: dataset spans two antigens (alpha beta) × three replicate plates , giving six curve_id values (1–6). alpha curves simulated Gompertz model; beta curves 5PL model, reflecting realistic -antigen variation curve shape.

title: Frequentist Calibration Curves with curveRfreq
text: curveRfreq preprocess data. transforms — concentration computation, prozone correction, blank handling, log10 transforms — must applied upstream via curveRcore::preprocess_standards() (component functions). clean separation means curveRfreq curveRbayes receive data identical fitting scale, making results directly comparable. preprocess_standards() applies steps order: compute_concentration() — converts dilution column absolute concentration using known undiluted standard concentration, optionally log10-transforming result. correct_prozone() — dampens hook (prozone) effect high concentrations compressing post-peak signal toward peak. perform_blank_operation() — applies one five blank strategies: "ignored" (default), "included" (append extra point), "subtracted", "subtracted_3x", "subtracted_10x". compute_log_response() — applies log10() response. Values ≤ 0 floored 1 % minimum positive value transformation. bead assay example, undiluted standard concentration 30 AU/mL (highest point dilution series stored dilution = 1/CONC): Key contract: preprocess_standards(), column named concentration holds log10-transformed concentration, response column (mfi ) holds log10-transformed MFI. scales fit_calibration_freq_multiplate() expects.
code: std_raw   <- bead_assay_example$standards blank_raw <- bead_assay_example$blanks  # Preprocess one curve at a time, then stack std_preprocessed <- do.call(rbind, lapply(   split(std_raw, std_raw$curve_id),   function(df) {     cid   <- df$curve_id[1]     blanks_for_curve <- blank_raw[blank_raw$curve_id == cid, ]     result <- curveRcore::preprocess_standards(       data                = df,       antigen_settings    = list(standard_curve_concentration = 30),       response_variable   = "mfi",       independent_variable = "concentration",       is_log_response     = TRUE,       blank_data          = blanks_for_curve,       blank_option        = "subtracted",       is_log_independent  = TRUE,       apply_prozone       = TRUE     )     result$data   } ))  # Both response and concentration are now on the log10 scale head(std_preprocessed[, c("curve_id", "concentration", "mfi")]) #>     curve_id concentration      mfi #> 1.1        1   -1.52287875 1.964654 #> 1.2        1   -1.04575749 2.476663 #> 1.3        1   -0.52287875 3.047580 #> 1.4        1   -0.04575749 3.616883 #> 1.5        1    0.47712125 4.094851 #> 1.6        1    0.95424251 4.276834

title: Frequentist Calibration Curves with curveRfreq
text: fit_calibration_freq_multiplate() recommended entry point. splits stacked preprocessed data curve_id, calls fit_calibration_freq() , collects results calibration_result_multiplate object, handles per-curve errors gracefully.

text: fit_ensemble_nls() fits model independently. model : Generates starting values generate_start_lists(). Candidate starts evenly spaced across parameter bounds: 3 starts "high" "medium" scale data. 5 starts "low" scale data, slope b biased toward lower end range (squared fractional spacing) avoid overshooting flat portion low-signal curves. Runs minpack.lm::nlsLM() start, keeping fit lowest AIC. Tighter tolerances (ftol = ptol = 1e-8, maxiter = 200) used low-signal data. Falls back primary starts fail scale class "low": Fallback 1 — relaxes bounds 50 % direction retries nlsLM midpoint. Fallback 2 — switches stats::nls() algorithm = "port" (box-constrained trust-region), can converge Levenberg-Marquardt . model exhausts fallbacks recorded converged = FALSE excluded downstream eligibility assessment selection.

title: Frequentist Calibration Curves with curveRfreq
text: log10-scale independent variable, pcov computed delta-method SE log10 scale: pcov=SEx×ln⁡(10)×100% \text{pcov} = \text{SE}_{x} \times \ln(10) \times 100 \% SEx2=∇θx⊤Σ∇θx+(∂x∂y)2σy2\text{SE}_x^2 = \nabla_\theta x^\top \Sigma \nabla_\theta x + \left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}\right)^2 \sigma_y^2 σy\sigma_y summary(fit)$sigma (residual SE response fitting scale). first term captures parameter uncertainty (propagated inverse function via curveRcore::make_inv_and_grad_fixed()), second captures observation-level noise.

title: Frequentist Calibration Curves with curveRfreq
text: every converged model grid, can compare precision profiles side side — even non-selected model: Precision profiles candidate models curve_id 1.
code: library(ggplot2)  grid_list <- lapply(names(cr1$ensemble), function(nm) {   g <- cr1$ensemble[[nm]]$grid   if (is.null(g) || !"x_fit" %in% names(g)) return(NULL)   g <- as.data.frame(g)  # explicit copy — prevents mutation of cr1$grid   g$model <- nm   g }) grid_compare <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), grid_list))  if (!is.null(grid_compare) && "x_fit" %in% names(grid_compare)) {   ggplot(grid_compare,          aes(x = x_fit, y = pcov, colour = model)) +     geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +     geom_hline(yintercept = 20, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +     annotate("text", x = -3.8, y = 22, label = "pcov threshold (20 %)",              hjust = 0, size = 3.2, colour = "grey40") +     scale_colour_manual(values = c(logistic4 = "#0072B2", gompertz4 = "#D55E00")) +     labs(x = "log10 concentration", y = "Percent CV (%)",          title = "Precision profiles — curve_id 1",          colour = "Model") +     theme_bw(base_size = 12) } else {   message("Skipping compare-grids plot: x_fit not available in ensemble grids.") } #> Warning: Removed 53 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_line()`).

code: best_grid <- as.data.frame(cr1$ensemble[[sel$best_model_name]]$grid) best_elig <- cr1$ensemble[[sel$best_model_name]]$eligibility  if ("d2y_dx2" %in% names(best_grid)) {   ok <- is.finite(best_grid$d2y_dx2)    ggplot(best_grid[ok, ],          aes(x = x_fit, y = d2y_dx2)) +     geom_line(colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 1) +     geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +     {if (is.finite(best_elig$shape_lloq_log10))       geom_vline(xintercept = best_elig$shape_lloq_log10,                  linetype = "dotted", colour = "#D55E00", linewidth = 0.8)} +     {if (is.finite(best_elig$shape_uloq_log10))       geom_vline(xintercept = best_elig$shape_uloq_log10,                  linetype = "dotted", colour = "#D55E00", linewidth = 0.8)} +     {if (is.finite(best_elig$shape_lloq_log10))       annotate("text", x = best_elig$shape_lloq_log10, y = max(best_grid$d2y_dx2[ok]) * 0.8,                label = "shape-LLOQ", hjust = -0.1, colour = "#D55E00", size = 3.5)} +     {if (is.finite(best_elig$shape_uloq_log10))       annotate("text", x = best_elig$shape_uloq_log10, y = min(best_grid$d2y_dx2[ok]) * 0.8,                label = "shape-ULOQ", hjust = 1.1, colour = "#D55E00", size = 3.5)} +     labs(x = "log10 concentration (AU/mL)",          y = expression(d^2*(log[10]*y) / d*(log[10]*x)^2),          title = paste("Second derivative profile —", sel$best_model_name, "— curve_id 1")) +     theme_bw(base_size = 12) }

text: $detection_limits element calibration_result contains three families metrics computed parameter confidence intervals: LODs (Limits Detection): upper 97.5% CI (lower LOD) lower 2.5% CI d (upper LOD), mapped response concentration scales. title: Frequentist Calibration Curves with curveRfreq
text: test sample, predict_samples_freq() applies analytical inverse best-fit model observed response: Log-transform raw response: y_fit = log10(max(mfi, 1e-6)). Invert forward model via closed-form inverse (e.g. 4PL: x=c+blog⁡y−ad−yx = c + b \log \frac{y - }{d - y}) obtain predicted_concentration log10 scale. Propagate uncertainty via delta method: Var(x)=∇θx⊤Σ∇θx+(∂x∂y)2σy2\text{Var}(x) = \nabla_\theta x^\top \Sigma \nabla_\theta x + \left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}\right)^2 \sigma_y^2, yielding se_concentration pcov. Recover pre-dilution concentration: final_concentration = 10^x * dilution. analytical inverse gradient functions reside curveRcore (inverses.R, gradients.R) selected via curveRcore::make_inv_and_grad_fixed(), returns list three closures (inv, grad, grad_y) built per model reused across samples.

title: Frequentist Calibration Curves with curveRfreq
text: vignette walked complete curveRfreq workflow: Ecosystem — curveRfreq frequentist fitting engine; depends curveRcore preprocessing, model definitions, inverses, gradients, calibration_result class. Preprocessing — curveRcore::preprocess_standards() transforms concentration response log10 scale handles blanks prozone effects fitting occurs. Fitting — fit_calibration_freq_multiplate() splits data curve_id fits ensemble NLS models per curve. NLS algorithm — multi-start Levenberg-Marquardt adaptive bounds; two fallback strategies low-signal data. Eligibility gates — four gates (at_bound, vcov_condition, rel_se, dynamic_range) intercept unidentified boundary-constrained models AIC ranking. Audit trail — $selection exposes gate results, AIC table, fallback status, distinction AIC winner eligibility-gated winner. Per-model grids — ensemble[[model]]$grid populated every converged model contains full precision profile (pcov, pcov_rmse, se_concentration). LLOQ / ULOQ — derived precision grid pcov_threshold; accessible ensemble[[model]]$eligibility. Second derivative shape-LOQ — d2y_dx2 column every grid; shape-LLOQ shape-ULOQ $eligibility bracket quasi-linear region maximum sensitivity. Detection limits — LODs, MDC, RDL $detection_limits, computed asymptote parameter CIs analytical inverse. Sample back-calculation — analytical inverse + delta-method uncertainty propagation; final_concentration includes dilution factor; pcov_pass flags whether sample falls within quantifiable range. Object structure — calibration_result standard S3 list; summary_table() collect_samples() extract tidy summaries multi-curve runs. ```

title: curveRfreq 0.1.0
text: Initial release. fit_calibration_freq() — single-curve NLS calibration multi-start Levenberg-Marquardt AIC + eligibility-gate selection. fit_calibration_freq_multiplate() — multi-curve wrapper splits curve_id handles per-curve errors gracefully. Per-model precision grids: every converged model gets full pcov profile, just selected best. Four eligibility gates: at_bound, vcov_condition, rel_se, dynamic_range — intercept unidentified models AIC ranking. summary_table() collect_samples() tidy extraction multi-curve results. bead_assay_example synthetic dataset two antigens × three plates.
